We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply. Your Role: We’re looking for a People Operations Partner to be a reliable, high-touch operator for our global workforce. You’ll own the day-to-day People Ops engine such as onboarding, offboarding, employee lifecycle transactions, data quality, and employee support while also stretching into employee relations support and cross-functional People projects as needed. This is a hands-on, execution-first role: roughly 70% core People Operations and 30% adjacent work (employee relations support, analytics, systems, and special projects). You’ll work across regions and time zones, not as a single-region specialist, and you’ll help keep our processes consistent, compliant, and human as we scale. If you like making operations feel invisible when they work and you’re curious about how AI and modern HR systems can take the busywork out of People work this role will fit. What you’ll do Process a high volume of employee lifecycle work such as onboarding, offboarding, transfers, job/comp changes, and related requests. Coordinate cross-functional follow-through so employees and managers get timely, high-quality support. Partner with employees and leaders across regions and time zones. Execute global People processes while navigating local nuances so support feels consistent and locally aware. Provide benefits support where needed, including answering employee questions, helping with enrollments or life event changes, and coordinating with vendors or specialists on more complex issues. Maintain accurate, audit-ready employee files and HRIS records. Flag data gaps, process breaks, and compliance risks early, and help keep the People tech stack running smoothly. Triage employee and manager questions on policies, processes, benefits, and systems. Know when to resolve it yourself, when to loop in Benefits/Payroll/Legal/IT, and when to escalate. Handle sensitive situations with discretion and sound judgment. Pull and clean reports from the HRIS and adjacent systems (headcount, starters/leavers, tenure, and other people metrics). Help maintain dashboards and turn raw data into clear, usable summaries for the People team and leadership. Support high-impact People initiatives: HRIS/ATS improvements, workflow redesign, policy rollouts, audit prep, and other cross-functional projects. Look for practical ways to use AI and automation to reduce manual work (FAQs, documentation, reporting, request triage, process mapping) while staying thoughtful about privacy, accuracy, and employee trust. What we’re looking for Required 1–3 years in People Operations, HR Operations, HR Coordinator/Generalist, or a closely related role Experience supporting the employee lifecycle (onboarding, offboarding, and day-to-day HR transactions) Comfort working with a global or multi-country workforce, or clear evidence you can learn local nuances quickly and operate across time zones Strong attention to detail, organization, and follow-through in a high-volume environment Clear, professional written and verbal communication including with employees and managers Discretion with confidential employee information Confidence in spreadsheets (Excel or Google Sheets) and HR systems; able to pull reports, spot data issues, and keep records clean A service mindset: you default to helpful, calm, and reliable, even when volume is high Comfort in a fast-moving environment: you can juggle competing priorities, stay composed when things are busy, and still deliver accurate work without losing the human touch Nice to have Hands-on experience with modern HRIS platforms such as HiBob, Rippling, Workday, BambooHR, or similar Exposure to employee relations (intake, documentation, case tracking, or supporting investigations) Experience supporting employee benefits (questions, enrollments, life events, or vendor coordination) Experience supporting systems or process projects (HRIS implementation, workflow redesign, audit, or policy rollout) Genuine interest in AI and how it can improve People operations (tools, prompts, automation, documentation) Startup, high-growth, or similarly fast-paced experience Experience in a remote or multi-entity environment How We Take Care of You: Competitive Salary & Stock Options Health Benefits New Hire Home-Office Setup: One-time USD $500 Monthly Stipend: USD $150 per month via a Brex Card Alpaca is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace dedicated to pursuing and hiring a diverse workforce. review_candidates.description: Functie inhoud Wanneer een kind een ouder heeft met een ernstige psychiatrische aandoening, zoals een bipolaire of psychotische aandoening, of ernstige depressie, heeft dit kind een 2 tot 4 maal groter risico om zelf psychiatrische problemen te ontwikkelen. We willen beter begrijpen hoe en wanneer (dit risico op) een ernstige psychiatrische aandoening ontstaat. We weten dat de (hersen)ontwikkeling van een kind tijdens de zwangerschap en de eerste twee jaar van het leven heel belangrijk is voor de rest van het leven. Maar we weten nog niet veel over hoe de hersenen van kinderen ontwikkelen in de baarmoeder. Ook weten we nog weinig over hoe pasgeboren baby's en jonge kinderen van ouders met een ernstige psychiatrische aandoening zich ontwikkelen. Daarnaast zijn er wereldwijd nog weinig gegevens bekend over de invloed van stress van ouders, kenmerken van het gezinsleven en de ouder-kindrelatie op de sociaalemotionele ontwikkeling van het kind in deze groep. Als we vroeg kunnen zien dat de ontwikkeling van deze kinderen anders verloopt, dan hopen we met goede begeleiding te voorkomen dat kinderen ziek worden of het tijdstip van mogelijk ziek worden uit te stellen. In de PANDA-studie volgen we de hersen- en sociaalemotionele ontwikkeling van ongeboren en pasgeboren kinderen van wie minimaal één ouder een ernstige psychiatrische aandoening heeft. Dit vergelijken we met kinderen van wie de ouders geen psychiatrische aandoening hebben. Ook bekijken we hoe kenmerken van de hersen- en sociaalemotionele ontwikkeling van het kind samenhangen met de ouder-kindrelatie. We brengen de hersenontwikkeling in kaart door MRI-scans te maken van baby's in de buik en pasgeborenen. En we volgen de sociaalemotionele ontwikkeling van het kind, de ouder-kind relatie en symptomen van ouders middels (online) vragenlijsten tot het kindje 18 maanden is. Daarnaast komen wij bij de gezinnen langs met de Sophia-bus wanneer het kindje 9 maanden is. Om het sociaal-emotioneel functioneren van het kind te meten middels eye-tracking, en om de ouder-kind relatie te observeren middels video-opnames van ouder-kind interacties. Als Onderzoeksmedewerker Ondersteun je de postdoctoraal onderzoeker en PhD student in het opzetten en uitvoering van het onderzoek. Ben je verantwoordelijk voor de werving, het plannen van afspraken, dataverzameling en dataverwerking. Ben je het aanspreekpunt van het project voor gezinnen. Neem je psychiatrische interviews af, help je bij het maken van MRI-scans van zwangeren en pasgeborenen, ga je samen met studenten met de Sophia-bus langs bij gezinnen om eye-tracking en interactietaken af te nemen. Begeleid je masterstudenten psychologie, pedagogiek of geneeskunde gedurende hun wetenschappelijke stage.

review_candidates.description: Overview The AFGHS-Jhpiego project is funded by the U.S. Department of State (DoS) to support the delivery of lifesaving, comprehensive maternal, newborn and child health (MNCH) and malaria services across Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar. It aims to improve service and data quality, strengthen health-system integration and resilience, facilitate effective transition, and promote local ownership and accountability for sustained health outcomes. Jhpiego works closely with the Ministries of Health in Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar, the Reproductive and Child Health Section (RCHS), the National Malaria Control Programme (NMCP), the Zanzibar Malaria Elimination Programme (ZAMEP), and Regional Administration and Local Government (RALG) structures to align implementation with national priorities and strengthen locally led implementation and oversight. The Lead Project Driver provides safe, reliable, and timely transport and logistics support to the project team by operating and maintaining an assigned project vehicle in a clean, safe, and roadworthy condition. The role supports transportation of staff, government counterparts, visitors, project materials, commodities, and other approved property for project activities and supports route planning, field logistics, vehicle documentation, and fuel management. Supervised by the Administrator and working under the functional guidance and mentorship of the Lead Driver, the Lead Project Driver operates in accordance with Jhpiego transport, Vehicle and Motorcycle Use, Fuel Use, road safety, maintenance, and other applicable policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs), as well as the Tanzania Road Traffic Act. The Project Lead Driver is responsible for the condition and appropriate use of the assigned vehicle, timely reporting of maintenance and safety concerns, accurate vehicle and fuel documentation, and responsible and cost-efficient use of project resources. The Lead Project Driver also supports field implementation and serves as an important point of observation during field travel and activities. The role is expected to demonstrate professionalism, accountability, confidentiality, and responsible stewardship of Jhpiego resources and to promptly report safety, compliance, or other questionable activities through established reporting channels. This position will be closed on October 12, 2026. Responsibilities 1. Transport Services and Route Planning Provide safe, reliable, and timely transport to staff, government counterparts, visitors, partners, and other authorized passengers for approved project activities. Support route planning, including departure times, travel duration, road conditions, fuel requirements, and arrival schedules, to ensure safe, timely, and cost-efficient travel. Support movement of project materials, equipment, commodities, and other approved property across assigned project geographies. Coordinate travel with the Administrator, Lead Driver, Field Team Lead, and relevant project staff to promote efficient vehicle utilization and minimize unnecessary travel and costs. 2. Vehicle Operation and Maintenance Operate the assigned project vehicle, fuel card, devices, and accessories strictly for approved purposes and in accordance with Jhpiego policies and SOPs. Ensure the assigned vehicle is clean, safe, properly maintained, and roadworthy at all times. Conduct required routine and monthly vehicle checks, complete vehicle checklists, and submit documentation within established timelines. Promptly report vehicle faults, maintenance requirements, accidents, damage, or other vehicle-related concerns to the Lead Driver and Administrator. Ensure required servicing and repairs are initiated through approved Jhpiego procedures and within required maintenance schedules. Monitor servicing and repair of the assigned vehicle and promptly report concerns regarding repair quality, parts used, costs, delays, or additional work proposed. Following servicing or repairs, check the vehicle and promptly report unresolved or recurring faults. Maintain required vehicle tools and emergency and safety equipment in accordance with Jhpiego SOPs. 3. Documentation, Fuel, Insurance, and Compliance Maintain complete and accurate mileage, trip, fuel, maintenance, and vehicle usage records, including required authorizations and passenger signatures. Use Jhpiego fuel cards and other fuel arrangements only for authorized purposes and complete fuel reconciliations accurately and within required timelines. Maintain a valid and current driving license and monitor insurance, registration, road safety inspection/sticker, and other required documentation for the assigned vehicle. Notify the Lead Driver and Administrator well in advance of expiry dates to prevent any lapse in vehicle insurance, registration, inspection, or other legally required documentation. Do not operate a vehicle with expired or lapsed insurance or other legally required documentation and immediately report any actual or anticipated lapse. Comply with Jhpiego transport, Vehicle and Motorcycle Use, Fuel Use, road safety, maintenance, documentation, and other applicable SOPs and requirements. 4. Safety, Conduct, and Accountability Observe all traffic laws, speed limits, road safety requirements, and defensive driving practices. Demonstrate professional conduct, courtesy, discretion, and respect when transporting staff, government counterparts, partners, visitors, and other passengers. Maintain confidentiality and safeguard passengers, project vehicles, equipment, commodities, documents, and other project property. Immediately report accidents, security concerns, unsafe road conditions, vehicle misuse, fuel misuse, or other risks through established reporting channels. Remain observant during travel and field activities and promptly report suspicious, unusual, or questionable activities, behaviors, transactions, or use of project resources through established Jhpiego reporting and escalation channels. Report concerns objectively and confidentially and do not independently investigate suspected misconduct. 5. Logistics and Field Activity Support Support organization, packing, transportation, set-up, and collection of materials and equipment for meetings, trainings, mentorship visits, and other field activities. Support receipt, collection, transportation, and delivery of project commodities and materials according to approved distribution plans and ensure required delivery documentation is completed and signed. As assigned and appropriately trained, support participant registration and other field implementation activities using approved Jhpiego systems and devices. As assigned and appropriately trained, support processing of approved field payments using Jhpiego's JEMS system in accordance with established authorization, documentation, financial control, and accountability requirements. Provide other basic administrative and logistical support during project-supported field activities as required. 6. Coordination and Operational Support Coordinate closely with the Administrator, Lead Driver, Field Team Lead, technical teams, and other drivers to align transport and logistics support with approved implementation schedules. Support inspection of hired vehicles and report concerns related to safety, roadworthiness, documentation, or compliance before use for project activities. Participate in driver briefings, meetings, coaching, refresher sessions, and other transport-related capacity strengthening as required. Participate in approved vehicle-sharing and car-pooling arrangements to promote efficient use of project transport resources. Provide transport and logistics support outside the assigned region when required and approved. 7. Sustainability and Responsible Resource Use Support efficient and cost-effective use of project vehicles, fuel, transport arrangements, and logistics resources. Coordinate transport and logistics arrangements with project and government teams, where appropriate, to reduce duplication and maximize available resources. Support project transition by working through existing regional and council logistics and implementation arrangements wherever feasible. Maintain accurate vehicle, fuel, maintenance, and logistics records to strengthen accountability, asset management, and responsible handover or transition of project resources. At least five years of professional driving experience; experience working with an international NGO or donor-funded project is desirable. Advanced Driver's Certificate from the National Institute of Transport (NIT) or other recognized Tanzanian institution is an added advantage. Basic knowledge of vehicle mechanics, preventive maintenance, and road safety. Experience supporting field activities in rural or hard-to-reach areas is desirable. Demonstrated understanding of safe vehicle operation, fuel accountability, and vehicle documentation. Professional, dependable, and able to interact effectively with government officials, staff, partners, and visitors. Ability to communicate effectively in Kiswahili and English. Basic computer and digital skills and ability to learn Jhpiego systems, including JEMS and other approved field systems. Willingness and ability to undertake regular travel within assigned project geographies and periodically support other project areas as required. Perform other duties assigned by the appropriate supervisor. Required Knowledge And Skills Strong communication and report-writing skills. Proactive, self-motivated, and able to work with minimal supervision. Experience in supervision, and quality improvement. Strong teamwork and interpersonal skills.
